assertions: The dog will be recovered and returned to its owner, not permanently lost
Search the western part of London, specifically the southern quarter verging west — south-westward from the querent's home at Temple Bar
The dog is still in London within the city, not gone far away or out of the city, as its significator is in a sign of the same triplicity as the ascendant signifying London

The dog is at first hidden or obscured from open view, kept in an enclosed or other person's place rather than roaming openly in the street, shown by the Moon in an airy sign under the Sun's beams and Sun and Moon in the 8th
Recovery or certain news of the dog comes on the following Monday, within days, as the Sun then applies by dexter aspect to Saturn, lord of the ascendant

Recovery comes by a harmonious, friendly contact rather than by loss or death of the animal, shown by the dog's significator applying to a trine of the cusp of the 6th house, and the dog is alive when found
method: Lilly classical horary astrology (6th-house animal significator, direction by sign and quarter, recovery by applying trine and Sun applying to lord of ascendant)
reasoning: Dog signified by 6th house and its lord. Its significator in a western sign gives west direction, in the southern quarter verging west gives south-west search area. Same triplicity as ascendant (London) keeps it in the city and near. Applying trine to 6th cusp is a favourable recovery aspect. Moon under beams with Sun and Moon in 8th shows initial concealment by another/in an obscure enclosed place, not open roaming. Sun applying on the following Monday by dexter aspect to Saturn, lord of ascendant/querent, fixes the timing in days to that Monday for news/return to the querent.
summary: He shall recover the dog: search west, in the southern quarter verging west of London, with news or return on the following Monday.
